Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was among the most brilliant in fifteenth-century Europe.

The last great Valois duke of Burgundy. He died outside Nancy in 1477; the French Crown incorporated the duchy, while his daughter Mary inherited rights over the Low Countries and Franche-Comté. The inheritance was disputed and did not remain a united state.

The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Low Countries and, after Senlis in 1493, Franche-Comté and Artois. He retained the ducal title of Burgundy although the duchy was under the French crown. His marriage to Joanna I brought him to Castile and transmitted distinct inheritances to Charles V.

Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He subsequently acquired Friesland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drenthe, Groningen and Guelders in stages between 1524 and 1543. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.
Ruler of the Spanish Monarchy when its European and Atlantic power was at its height. His reign saw Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great revolt of the Low Countries.
He ruled the Netherlands with Isabella Clara Eugenia. His regime sought to stabilize the Catholic territories and coincided with the Twelve-Year Truce.
She exercised the sovereignty of the Netherlands with Alberto and then continued as governor. Her political role was much broader than that of a dynastic consort.

people.nombre: Charles VI of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: A Habsburg emperor and Philip V’s rival in the War of the Spanish Succession. His house governed Milan, Naples and Sardinia at different dates; he exchanged Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance for Maria Theresa.

Ruler of the Habsburg hereditary lands and one of the great figures of the eighteenth century. She defended her inheritance in the War of the Austrian Succession and introduced important administrative reforms.

people.nombre: Joseph II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: A Habsburg emperor associated with enlightened absolutism. He sought a profound modernisation of the administration, Church and society of his territories through an ambitious reform programme.

people.nombre: Leopold II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: A Habsburg emperor whose brief reign followed his government of Tuscany. He moderated several of Joseph II’s reforms and confronted the spread of the French Revolution in Europe.

people.nombre: Francis II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: The last Holy Roman Emperor and the first Emperor of Austria from 1804. He fought revolutionary and Napoleonic France, dissolved the Empire in 1806 and married his daughter Marie Louise to Napoleon.
Consort of the Brabant dynasty. Their life was connected with Brabant, Savoy.

He inherited Brabant as a minor, under the government of his mother Adelaide. In 1267 he gave up the duchy and the succession passed to his brother John I. His brief stage avoids turning Henry III's reversion to John I into an immediate continuity that did not occur.

He succeeded John I in Brabant and Limburg, married Margaret of England and fathered John III. The marriage maintained the duchy’s English connection, while the two ducal dignities continued to pass together within one house.

Daughter of Edward I and Leonor of Castile, she married John II of Brabant. She was the mother of John III. Through her, the Brabantinea ducal line was connected to England and Castile before her subsequent relationship with the Valois of Burgundy.

He ruled Brabant and Limburg during the first half of the 14th century. His daughters Juana and Margarita brought family rights to different paths. Juana's succession and Margaret's Flemish marriage prepared the challenges and agreements that brought his duchy closer to the Burgundy.

people.nombre: María de Évre, Duchess of Brabant
people.dinastia: A Capetian branch whose French patrimony became the starting point of a long royal history in Navarre.
people.resumen: Daughter of Louis of Évreux and Margaret of Artois, she married John III of Brabant. She was the mother of Joanna of Brabant and Margaret, wife of Louis II of Flanders. Her descendants connected the Brabantine and Flemish successions with the Capetian branch of Évreux.
Duke of Brabant who took part in the Hundred Years’ War and died at Agincourt. His position linked the Burgundian inheritance with the Low Countries.

First wife of Antonio de Borgoña, she was mother of John IV of Brabant and Philip of Saint-Pol. His two sons successively occupied the ducates of Brabant and Limburg. The absence of offspring from both of them opened his inheritance to his cousin Philip the Good.

He inherited Brabant and married Jacqueline of Bavaria. The marriage involved him in the conflict over Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut, but did not bring those inheritances permanently under his control. His brother Philip of Saint-Pol succeeded him.

He succeeded his brother John IV in Brabant and Limburg. He died childless, and the duchies passed to Philip the Good, cousin of both brothers. This succession brought the Brabantine inheritance into the Burgundian dominions.

name: Castile
summary: The Spanish kingdom went from sharing and disputing the Lion heritage to leading an extensive peninsular monarchy. Since 1230 it has been permanently sharing monarch with Leon, although both names and their legal traditions continued to exist.

uniones.resumen: Ferdinand III gathered two legacies. The continuity of a common monarch did not immediately erase the legal identities and traditions of the kingdoms.
uniones.instituciones: The Crown of Castile was a composite structure in evolution. Castile, Leon and Spain are not three equivalent or interchangeable kingdoms in filters.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: the Great Captain changes the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French in Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, field fortification and firearms consolidates the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance born of the 1500 cast is definitely broken in favour of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Ferdinand gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Ferdinand the Catholic as king of Naples in addition to Trinacria. The two parts of the former Sicilian monarchy once again share sovereign, although they will continue to be administered as distinct kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

eventos.descripcion: Poland and Lithuania move from a dynastic union to a narrower political community. The new structure will survive the male extinction of the Jagellon and make possible a common elective monarchy.
After the death without heirs of Segismundo II Augusto, the nobility chooses Henry of Valois and sets permanent limits to real power through the Henrician Articles.

eventos.titulo: Ana Jagelón and Esteban Bathory share the crown
eventos.descripcion: The election of Esteban Bathory with Ana Jagelón shows that dynastic legitimacy continues to matter, but it is no longer enough on its own: the crown depends on the election of the nobility.

eventos.titulo: A Vasa is elected king of Poland
eventos.descripcion: Segismund III Vasa arrives at the Polish-Lithuanian crown as grandson of Sigismund I and Swedish prince. The election opens a stage in which the Commonwealth crosses directly with the dynastic struggles of the Baltic.
After decades of wars and crisis, John II Casimir leaves the throne. The nobility can re-elect from scratch and leans towards a candidate born within the Commonwealth itself.

The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburgenic and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. Victory opens a new phase of the war in Hungary and reinforces the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Augustus the Fort gets the crown
eventos.descripcion: The Elector of Saxony converts to Catholicism and succeeds in being elected king. Poland-Lithuania is personally united to Saxony and his election turns the crown back into a European issue.

eventos.titulo: Two elections for a single crown
eventos.descripcion: Estanislao Leszczyński and Augusto III are proclaimed by rival factions. The dispute leads to a European war and shows how far neighbouring powers can condition electoral freedom.

eventos.titulo: The Last King of the Republic
eventos.descripcion: Stanislaus Augusto Poniatowski is elected king with a reformist program, but under the decisive shadow of Russia. The tension between nobility freedom, reform and external intervention enters its final phase.

eventos.titulo: May 3 Constitution tries to change the system
eventos.descripcion: The new constitution eliminates the veto liberum and replaces the elective monarchy with an inherited succession foreseen in the house of Saxony. It is the most ambitious attempt to reform the Republic from within.

eventos.titulo: Third partition ends with the Commonwealth
eventos.descripcion: The third partition erases the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from the political map and forces Stanislaus Augusto to abdicate. The chosen crown experiment ends under pressure from neighbouring monarchies.
Luis de Condé dies after the battle of Jarnac. Gaspar de Coligny remains as the chief Huguenot military chief while the Duke of Anjou, future Henry III, gains prestige in the Catholic camp.

The death of Francisco de Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guise reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
The Day of Barricades forces Henry III to leave Paris and shows that the League and Henry of Guise can directly challenge the king in their own capital.

eventos.titulo: Henry III makes the Duke of Guise kill
eventos.descripcion: Fearing to lose control of the monarchy, Henry III ordered the death of Enrique de Guise in Blois. Carlos de Mayenne collected the military leadership of the League and the war entered its final phase.

Henry III is killed after having allied with Henry of Navarre against the League. With his death the Valois-Angulema line on the throne is extinguished and Henry of Navarre claims the crown as Henry IV.

eventos.titulo: Leopoldo and Sobieski agree to mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must turn to the aid of the ally.

eventos.titulo: Poles, Imperials and German Princes Gather
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces and joins contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and assumes command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to going on the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League was formed. Habsburg, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.

summary: The Basarab governments combined family rights, support from the boyars and intervention from neighboring powers. Vlad Călugărul and Radu the Great allow a line to continue different from Vlad III. Mircea Ciobanul's marriage to Chiajna Rareș connects the court with Moldova, keeping the two principalities separate.

name: Denmark
summary: The Danish monarchy articulated a network of unions and rivalries with Norway, Sweden and the Baltic principalities. From the daughters of Valdemar IV to the Oldenburgs, elections, marriages and wars produced shared crowns without a single succession for all kingdoms.

uniones.resumen: Olaf's inheritance linked two crowns that, with crises and dynastic changes, remained associated for centuries.
uniones.instituciones: Norway retained its own legal identity. Its position was more subordinated to Denmark with the reorganization of 1536–1537; personal union and composite monarchy do not describe exactly the same phase.

etapas.texto: Olaf inherited Norway from his father. His mother Margaret ruled during the minority.

personas.nombre: Olaf II of Denmark and IV of Norway
personas.resumen: Son of Margaret and Haakon VI. He was elected king of Denmark as a child and inherited Norway when his father died. His mother led the government. Olaf's death without descent in 1387 forced another successor solution and opened the way to recognition of Margaret and Erik of Pomerania.

The son of Magnus Eriksson and Blanca de Namur. He ruled Norway and briefly shared Swedish royalty with his father. He married Margaret, daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark. His son Olaf inherited Norway when he was already Danish king: the marriage prepared a union whose access occurred on different dates.

Queen and regent who gathered Denmark, Norway and Sweden under his authority and laid the foundations of the Kalmar Union. He was the dominant political figure of northern Europe at the end of the 14th century.

etapas.texto: Cristian I consolidated the link after the competition with Carlos Knutsson.

personas.resumen: Count of Oldenburg elected king of Denmark in 1448. He then gathered Norway and, for a shorter period, Sweden.
Charles Knutsson of Bonde's house alternated stages as king of Sweden with exiles and restorations. He also claimed and briefly exercised Norwegian royalty in front of Cristian I.

etapas.texto: The imposition of the Reform strengthened the Danish monarchy's control over Norway.

personas.resumen: The son of Frederick I. His victory in the war of the Count consolidated the monarchy and made possible the establishment of the Lutheran Reformation. Norway’s reorganization reinforced its subordination to the Danish crown. The continuity of the common monarch thus lived with a profound change in institutions.

etapas.texto: The treaty of Kiel broke the union. Norway approved a constitution and, after a conflict with Sweden, entered another union with modifications.

personas.resumen: He exercised the regency for years before succeeding Cristian VII. Napoleonic wars ended with the loss of Norway in 1814. The cession agreed upon in Kiel did not produce a peaceful and immediate transfer to Sweden: there was a Norwegian constitutional movement, a war and a new agreement.

He acceded to the Swedish throne after the deposition of Gustav IV Adolfo. Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte’s adoption resolved the search for an heir. In 1814 he also became king of Norway after the war and the constitutional agreement; the new union retained Norwegian institutions of its own.

uniones.resumen: Erik's coronation in Kalmar expressed the project of a common monarch. Sweden repeatedly passed between union kings, own kings and regencies.
uniones.instituciones: The three kingdoms retained their own laws and councils. Kalmar was neither a unitary state nor an uninterrupted succession of common kings.

etapas.texto: Erik was crowned in Kalmar. Margarita continued to exercise decisive authority.

personas.resumen: Nephew grandson of Margaret, he was promoted as heir and recognized in the three kingdoms before the coronation of Kalmar in 1397. Margaret continued to lead politics until 1412.

Queen and regent who gathered Denmark, Norway and Sweden under his authority and laid the foundations of the Kalmar Union. He was the dominant political figure of northern Europe at the end of the 14th century.

etapas.texto: The revolt against Erik opened a phase of regency, restoration and deposition.

personas.resumen: Nephew grandson of Margaret, he was promoted as heir and recognized in the three kingdoms before the coronation of Kalmar in 1397. Margaret continued to lead politics until 1412.
Charles Knutsson of Bonde's house alternated stages as king of Sweden with exiles and restorations. He also claimed and briefly exercised Norwegian royalty in front of Cristian I.

etapas.texto: Christopher of Bavaria completed his access to the three kingdoms.

personas.resumen: Erik's nephew of Pomerania by his mother Catherine. He was elected separately in Denmark, Sweden and Norway after his uncle's deposition. He married Dorothea of Brandenburg and died without children. The new crisis allowed the crowns to initially take different paths.

etapas.texto: The victory of Sten Sture the Elder in Brunkeberg strengthened the Swedish government against Cristian I.

personas.resumen: Regent of Sweden in two periods, he maintained a wide autonomy against the kings of the union. His victory at Brunkeberg in 1471 strengthened that position. King John's entry in 1497 interrupted his government, which he regained in 1501. His name should not be confused with Sten Sture the Younger.
Count of Oldenburg elected king of Denmark in 1448. He then gathered Norway and, for a shorter period, Sweden.

etapas.texto: Cristian II took Stockholm. The executions aggravated the opposition to his authority.

personas.resumen: He tried to strengthen the royal power in the Scandinavian kingdoms. Stockholm’s bloodbath intensified Swedish resistance and contributed to the breakup of the union.

Wife of Sten Sture the Younger. After the death of her husband in 1520 she led the Stockholm resistance against Cristian II and negotiated his capitulation. She was imprisoned after the conquest. Her son Svante extended the presence of the Sture in the nobility of the Swedish Vasa.

etapas.texto: Gustavo Vasa was elected king of Sweden. Denmark and Norway remained linked.

personas.resumen: Founder of the Vasa dynasty and builder of the modern Swedish state. He broke the Kalmar Union, promoted the Reformation and reinforced the royal authority over nobility and the Church.

Noble of the Anjou-Hungary dynasty. Their life is linked to Hungary, Silesia.
Duke of the Piast dynasty. Their life is linked to Silesia.

Emperor of the house of Luxembourg and king of Bohemia, he made Prague one of the great political and cultural centres of Europe. The Golden Bull of 1356 ordered the imperial election in a lasting way.
He was king of Bohemia and king of Romans, although the voters dismissed him from this second position. Religious and political tensions of his time preceded the Hussite wars.
Brother of Charles V and founder of the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs. He reunited Austria, Bohemia and much of Hungary and succeeded his brother in imperial dignity.
He strengthened the Hungarian army and administration and disputed territories to the Habsburgs and the Jagellons. His library and court made Buda a center of Renaissance humanism.
He united the crowns of Bohemia and Hungary under the Jagellon house. The growing noble influence limited his ability to act in both kingdoms.
He collected rights over Austria, Hungary and Bohemia after the death of Sigismund. He was elected King of Romans, but died without receiving imperial coronation.
He was born after the death of his father, Albert II, and inherited rights in several Central European territories. His minority turned the effective exercise of power into a subject of dispute.

eventos.descripcion: The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.

In the midst of the Austrian War of Succession, elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtains the imperial crown and demonstrates that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg dominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I opens the Habsburg-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francisco Esteban returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Teresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeds his father as emperor and, after 1780, tries to quickly reform the Habsburg domains, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France upsets the European political balance and makes the fate of Marie Antoinette, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrives, the old Empire still exists, but faces a transformation that will culminate a few years later.

The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburgenic and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. Victory opens a new phase of the war in Hungary and reinforces the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Third partition ends with the Commonwealth
eventos.descripcion: The third partition erases the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from the political map and forces Stanislaus Augusto to abdicate. The chosen crown experiment ends under pressure from neighbouring monarchies.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to the Sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of Leopoldo I’s monarchy is mixed with imperial rivalry in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopoldo and Sobieski agree to mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must turn to the aid of the ally.

The great Visir Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense while the fortifications suffer weeks of siege and minework.

eventos.titulo: Poles, Imperials and German Princes Gather
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces and joins contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and assumes command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to going on the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League was formed. Habsburg, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.
The conquest of Buda shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war begun in 1683 becomes a Habsburgic expansion by Hungary and permanently alters the balance of Central Europe.

people.resumen: King of Hungary and Bohemia and subsequently emperor. His involvement in the Great Schism, the Hussite Wars and the Council of Constance made him a central figure in fifteenth-century Europe.
His marriage to Elizabeth of Bohemia established the Luxembourgs on the throne in Prague. He campaigned throughout Europe and died at Crécy after losing his sight.

King of Bohemia and King of the Romans, although the electors deposed him from the latter office. The religious and political tensions of his time preceded the Hussite Wars.

He strengthened the Hungarian army and administration and contested territories with the Habsburgs and Jagiellonians. His library and court made Buda a centre of Renaissance humanism.
He united the crowns of Bohemia and Hungary under the Jagiellons. The nobility’s growing influence limited his freedom of action in both kingdoms.
He acquired claims to Austria, Hungary and Bohemia after Sigismund’s death. He was elected King of the Romans but died before receiving an imperial coronation.
Born after his father Albert II’s death, he inherited rights in several Central European territories. His minority made the effective exercise of power a matter of dispute.
A Habsburg emperor with a relatively conciliatory outlook in a Europe divided by the Reformation. He also ruled Bohemia and Hungary within his house’s complex Central European monarchy.
A Habsburg emperor who gradually took power from his brother Rudolf II. His reign set the stage for the dynastic and religious crisis that led to the Thirty Years’ War.

people.resumen: A Habsburg emperor and fervent defender of Catholicism. The Bohemian rebellion against his authority triggered the Thirty Years’ War, which transformed the Holy Roman Empire’s political map.
He died in the defeat at Mohács against Suleiman the Magnificent. His death opened a contest between Ferdinand of Habsburg and John Zápolya for the Hungarian crown.
A leading Hussite ruler from the Bohemian nobility who became king of Bohemia. He sought to maintain a difficult religious and diplomatic balance in fifteenth-century central Europe.
Elector Palatine and King of Bohemia during the winter of 1619–1620. His acceptance of the Bohemian crown turned a constitutional crisis into one of the triggers of the Thirty Years’ War.

Ruler of the Habsburg hereditary lands and one of the great figures of the eighteenth century. She defended her inheritance in the War of the Austrian Succession and introduced important administrative reforms.

King of Prussia from 1797. After Napoleon defeated Prussia at Jena in 1806, he supported the reforms of Stein and Hardenberg and joined the coalition that defeated France in 1813–1815.

uniones.titulo: The Burgundian inheritance, feuded to feud
uniones.resumen: Marriage, succession, purchase, renunciation and conquest gathered different legal fiefdoms. The map must follow each effective government, not paint all domains since the ducal investiture.
uniones.instituciones: Dijon's duchy was a French fief; the Franche Condado, an imperial fiefdom. Nevers and Rethel followed a smaller branch. After 1477, France took the duchy; the claims of Mary and her heirs do not amount to possession.

etapas.titulo: The Duchy of Philip the Bold
etapas.texto: The French Duchy was centered on Dijon. The counties of the north and the Franco Condado would arrive by Margarita III.

personas.resumen: He received the Duchy of Burgundy from his father, John II of France. His marriage to Margarita de Flanders laid the foundations for the burgundy expansion in the Netherlands.
Countess of Artois, 1361–1382. Countess of the Capetians dynasty.
Louis de Male, Count of Flanders since 1346. Faced with the Flemish cities, his daughter Margarita brought Flanders to the Dukes of Burgundy.

etapas.texto: Flanders, Artois and the Franche Condado joined by Margaret's hereditary right; their children received Nevers and Rethel as apanages before 1405.

personas.resumen: Louis de Male, Count of Flanders since 1346. Faced with the Flemish cities, his daughter Margarita brought Flanders to the Dukes of Burgundy.
Heir of Flanders, Artois and Burgundy County, he married Philip the Bold, Duke of Burgundy in 1369. His inheritance was the basis of the great burgundy state of his descendants.
He received the Duchy of Burgundy from his father, John II of France. His marriage to Margarita de Flanders laid the foundations for the burgundy expansion in the Netherlands.
Duke of Burgundy and protagonist of the French civil war. He ordered the murder of Louis of Orleans and ended up murdered in Montereau, feeding the Borgonian alliance with England.

The son of Philip the Bold and Margaret of Flanders, inherited Brabant and Limburg in 1406. The connection came from the brabanon ancestry of his mother. He died in Azincourt; his sons John IV and Philip of Saint-Pol later ruled before the inheritance of Philip the Good.
Count of Nevers, 1404–1415. Count of the Valois-Borgogna dynasty.

etapas.texto: Philip the Good took Namur in 1429 and inherited Brabant and Limburg in 1430.

personas.resumen: Count of Namur, 1418–1429. Count of the Dampierre dynasty.

He succeeded his brother John IV in Brabant and Limburg. He died without issue and the duchies passed to their cousin Philip the Good. This succession added a distinct Brabantine inheritance to the wider Burgundian possessions.
Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was one of the brightest in 15th century Europe.

etapas.texto: After the regency agreed at Delft, Jacqueline relinquished Holland, Hainaut and Zeeland in 1433.

personas.resumen: He inherited Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland from his father and defended his rights against John of Bavaria and Philip the Good. Their marriages were part of that political struggle. Delft's agreement of 1428 restricted his power and the 1433 cession incorporated the counties into the Burgundian heritage.
Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was one of the brightest in 15th century Europe.

etapas.texto: The purchase of 1441 rights and the takeover of the city in 1443 completed another gradual incorporation.

personas.resumen: Duchess of Luxembourg, 1411–1443. Duchess of the Luxembourg dynasty.
Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was one of the brightest in 15th century Europe.

etapas.texto: Charles the Temerary died, Mary retained the Netherlands; France took the duchy and contested Artois and the Franche Condado.

personas.resumen: Last Grand Duke Valois of Burgundy. He died before Nancy in 1477; the French Crown incorporated the duchy, while his daughter Mary inherited rights over the Netherlands and the Franche Condado. The inheritance was disputed and did not remain as a united state.

Heir to Charles the Temerary since 1477 and Duchess titular of Burgundy. His marriage to Maximilian of Habsburg linked that house to the Netherlands of Burgundy. The dispute with France over the duchy, the Franche Condado and Artois prevents presenting all the inheritance as territory that ruled without interruption.
Emperor Habsburg whose marriage policy laid the foundations for the extraordinary dynastic expansion of his house throughout Europe.

etapas.texto: Artois and the Franche Condado returned to the house of Austria; Philip I and Charles V transmitted them to the Netherlands.

personas.resumen: The son of Maria de Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Netherlands and, after Senlis (1493), the Franche Condado and Artois. He preserved the dignity of Duke of Burgundy, although the duchy was under the French Crown. His marriage to Juana I took him to Castile and transmitted heritages other than Charles V.

Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche Condado, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Güeldres in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. Since 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

eventos.descripcion: Juan Sin Miedo is murdered in Montereau. Felipe the Good inherits Burgundy and approaches the English side.
Joan is captured by Burgundian forces near Compiègne and ends up in English hands; she will be executed in Rouen in 1431.

eventos.titulo: Foundation of the Order of the Golden Toison
eventos.descripcion: Philip the Good founded the Order of the Golden Toison in the context of his marriage to Isabella of Portugal.
Philip the Good reconciles with Charles VII and breaks his alliance with England.
Charles the Temerario succeeds Philip the Good and tries to consolidate a territorial block between France and the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Battle of Nancy and death of Charles the Fearer
eventos.descripcion: Charles dies without a male heir. His daughter Maria receives an inheritance immediately disputed by Louis XI of France.
Marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returns Artois and the Franche Condado to the inheritance of Maria de Burgundy, while the Duchy of Burgundy remains in French hands.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected king of Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial election a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.

In the midst of the Austrian War of Succession, elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtains the imperial crown and demonstrates that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg dominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I opens the Habsburg-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francisco Esteban returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Teresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeds his father as emperor and, after 1780, tries to quickly reform the Habsburg domains, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France upsets the European political balance and makes the fate of Marie Antoinette, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrives, the old Empire still exists, but faces a transformation that will culminate a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents Charles V with a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Escaleld League and captures its two great leaders, but military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.

The death of Francisco de Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guise reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

people.resumen: Heir to Charles the Bold from 1477 and titular Duchess of Burgundy. Her marriage to Maximilian of Habsburg linked his house to the Burgundian Netherlands. Disputes with France over the duchy, Franche-Comté and Artois mean that the entire inheritance cannot be presented as territory she governed continuously.
Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was among the most brilliant in fifteenth-century Europe.

The last great Valois duke of Burgundy. He died outside Nancy in 1477; the French Crown incorporated the duchy, while his daughter Mary inherited rights over the Low Countries and Franche-Comté. The inheritance was disputed and did not remain a united state.

The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Low Countries and, after Senlis in 1493, Franche-Comté and Artois. He retained the ducal title of Burgundy although the duchy was under the French crown. His marriage to Joanna I brought him to Castile and transmitted distinct inheritances to Charles V.

Holy Roman Emperor and sovereign of a composite monarchy extending across the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Low Countries and the Americas. From Philip I he inherited Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur, Luxembourg and other Netherlandish territories. He subsequently acquired Friesland, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drenthe, Groningen and Guelders in stages between 1524 and 1543. He retained the title of Duke of Burgundy but did not govern the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; Philip II’s later investiture and possession must be distinguished from that government.
Ruler of the Spanish Monarchy when its European and Atlantic power was at its height. His reign saw Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great revolt of the Low Countries.

King of Spain during a period of great cultural brilliance and serious political crises. His reign, associated with the Count-Duke of Olivares, was marked by European wars and the revolts in Catalonia and Portugal.
The last Habsburg king of Spain. His lack of descendants turned the succession into a European question and, after his death, triggered the War of the Spanish Succession.

The first Bourbon king of Spain. The War of the Spanish Succession cost him Milan, Naples and Sardinia; he briefly recovered Sardinia between 1717 and 1720. His Iberian and Italian domains followed different paths.

Ruler of the Habsburg hereditary lands and one of the great figures of the eighteenth century. She defended her inheritance in the War of the Austrian Succession and introduced important administrative reforms.

people.nombre: Joseph II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: A Habsburg emperor associated with enlightened absolutism. He sought a profound modernisation of the administration, Church and society of his territories through an ambitious reform programme.

people.nombre: Leopold II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: A Habsburg emperor whose brief reign followed his government of Tuscany. He moderated several of Joseph II’s reforms and confronted the spread of the French Revolution in Europe.

name: Venice
summary: Venice was a republic governed by aristocratic institutions and by a chosen dogo. The succession of Atlas dogos allows to follow the position between 1400 and 1605; the domains of the republic were neither personal nor family heritage of the magistrate. Years of vacation and territorial changes are recorded separately.
notes: The dogo is an elected magistrate, not owner of the domains of the Republic. The map offers documented regional courts, without equated Istria, Dalmatia or the whole of the Ionian Islands with complete Venetian possessions.

eventos.descripcion: The fleet of the Holy League, led by Don Juan of Austria and composed mainly of forces of the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States, defeats the Ottoman navy of Ali Bajá after hours of galley combat against galley. The Ottoman center collapses, Uluç Ali manages to save part of his wing and thousands of fighters are killed, wounded or captives. Victory does not drive the Ottoman Empire out of the Mediterranean, but destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic triumph of the coalition.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrives, the old Empire still exists, but faces a transformation that will culminate a few years later.

eventos.titulo: The invasion of Cyprus forces Venice to seek allies
eventos.descripcion: The Ottoman offensive against Cyprus threatens one of the great Venetian possessions of the Levant. Venice needs to turn its particular war into a broader coalition.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

In Messina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetians, pontificals, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

The League has Barbarigo on the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Alvaro de Bazán on the front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá runs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali commands the wing that confronts Doria.

In the center, the Royal Gallery of Don Juan and the Sultan of Ali Bajá are locked in a struggle of approaches, archabuces and successive reinforcements. Ali Bajá's fall and the taking of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make the central combat the symbolic nucleus of victory.

eventos.titulo: The wings almost changed the result
eventos.descripcion: Barbarigo is mortally wounded in the Christian left wing. At the opposite end, Uluç Ali takes advantage of the open space during Doria's maneuver and hits several League galleys. Alvaro de Bazán's reserve comes to close the gap, while Uluç Ali manages to withdraw with part of his boats.
Venice signs peace with the Ottoman Empire and renounces Cyprus. Lepanto has been an extraordinary naval victory, but not an Ottoman expulsion from the Mediterranean: the strategic balance continues.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabel of Castile and Fernando of Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberian peninsula without legally merging them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada to Isabella I and Fernando II puts an end to the Nasrid emirate; Muhammad XII, Boabdil, gives the city.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected king of Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial election a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents Charles V with a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Escaleld League and captures its two great leaders, but military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.

The death of Francisco de Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guise reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

Alfonso V of Aragon defeats the Angevin resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since Vespers, the same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the continental kingdom, although the crowns retain separate identities.

eventos.titulo: Alfonso's inheritance is once again separated
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragon and Trinacria pass to their brother John II, while Naples remains for his son Fernando. Personal union does not become a stable fusion of crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Ferdinand the Catholic agree to divide the kingdom of Frederick I. Cooperation lasts little: disputes over the boundaries of partition make the former allies enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: the Great Captain changes the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French in Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, field fortification and firearms consolidates the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance born of the 1500 cast is definitely broken in favour of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Ferdinand gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Ferdinand the Catholic as king of Naples in addition to Trinacria. The two parts of the former Sicilian monarchy once again share sovereign, although they will continue to be administered as distinct kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

Mary and Martin arrived in Sicily with Aragonese support to impose themselves on the Barons. The Queen’s hereditary legitimacy was not enough without military capacity. The island’s government was once again closely linked to the Crown of Aragon.

Daughter of Hetum I and wife of Bohemundo VI. Her marriage reinforced the alliance between Armenia, Antioch and Tripoli; after the death of her husband she intervened in county politics during the Bohemundo VII minority.

He was elected king while imprisoned in Genoa. His release and return required concessions that preserved the island’s commercial dependence. After Leo V’s death, he added the nominal crown of Armenia to his titles.

Born while his parents were imprisoned in Genoa, he sought to regain room for manoeuvre against the Genoese. The Mamluk invasion of 1426 led to his capture and the imposition of tribute. His children connected Cyprus with Savoy and continued the dynasty.

He governed an island paying tribute to the Mamluks, with Famagusta in Genoese hands. His marriage to Helena Palaeologina strengthened Greek influences at court. His children Charlotte and James subsequently contested the succession.

An illegitimate son of John II, he secured Mamluk assistance to contest Charlotte’s crown and recovered Famagusta from the Genoese. His marriage to Catherine Cornaro strengthened Venetian influence. He died before his heir was born.

He transformed the rumenid principality into a monarchy recognized by the coronation of 1198. He negotiated with crusades, Byzantius and Muslim powers to sustain his position. His daughter Elizabeth inherited the crown and connected his succession with the Hitumids.

people.nombre: Sibylla of Lusignan, Queen of Armenia
people.resumen: The daughter of Amalarico of Lusignan and Elizabeth of Jerusalem, married Lion I of Armenia. She was the mother of Elizabeth, a heiress of the Cilicia crown. This link establishes a direct connection between the first royal houses in Cyprus, Jerusalem and Armenia.

He inherited his crown as a child and was the subject of dispute over his control of the kingdom. His first marriage with Philip of Antioch ended violently and his subsequent link with Hetum established a new dynasty. His own rights are preserved in succession.

people.nombre: Philip of Antioch, King of Armenia
people.resumen: Son of Bohemond IV, he gained the crown through his marriage to Isabella. Opposition among part of the Armenian nobility to his policies ended in his deposition and imprisonment. His fall opened the way for Isabella’s marriage to Hethum.

The great Armenian man and father of Hetum I, his father, had a central role in the crisis that brought his son to his throne. His family's marriage policy united his continuity with the predominance of the Hitumids.

Son of Hethum I and Isabella, he was held captive after the Mamluk invasion of 1266. As king he continued to seek Mongol support against Egypt. His many children linked Cilician Armenia with Byzantium and the Lusignans.

A wife of Lion II and mother of a great and true offspring, she appears with his family in a famous image of an Armenian manuscript. His sons occupied the crown or established links with Byzantius and Cyprus, giving this generation a great Mediterranean projection.

He alternated the crown with religious retirement and shared power with relatives. He sought a Mongol alliance against the Mamluks, but a Mongol commander killed him alongside his nephew Leo. His restorations have separate entries.

He received the throne after his brother Hethum withdrew and later shared power with him. The dispute between the brothers ended with his deposition and death in captivity. His son Leo recovered the rights of their line.

people.nombre: Margarita de Lusignan, Queen of Armenia
people.resumen: The daughter of Hugo III of Cyprus and his wife Teodor III of Armenia, was the mother of Leo III. Her marriage was one of the direct links between the two monarchies, prior to his entrance to the cilicia crown.

He took advantage of his brothers’ absence to seize the crown. Internal struggles weakened the kingdom’s position against its neighbours and ended with his deposition. His brief rule formed part of the succession crisis among the sons of Leo II.
He moved his brother Smbat and briefly occupied his crown before devoting his power to Hetum II. His reign was another phase of a dynastic dispute involving several sons of Leo II.

Son of Theodore III, he acceded to the throne under the tutelage of his uncle Hetum II. Both were killed by Mongolian chief Bilarghu. The crisis showed that the alliance with the Mongols did not guarantee the security of the Armenian monarchy.

Brother of Hetum II, he obtained the crown after the murders of 1307. He tried to hold the kingdom between the Mameluca threat and the search for Western support. The discussions on religious union accompanied his foreign policy.

He inherited the crown as a child, under a regency that accumulated great power. His search for Latin help and the struggles with nobility made instability worse. He died without an heir who maintained the male line of the Hitumidas.

people.nombre: Elizabeth of Armenia, wife of Amalaric
people.resumen: The daughter of Leo II and Karan married Amalaric of Lusignan. Following her husband's death his family became trapped in the struggles of the Armenian court. His descendants inherited the purport that brought the Lusignan to the Cilician throne.

Born Guido de Lusignan, she accepted the crown after her cousin Leo IV's death. Her project of bringing her closer to the Latin Church found resistance among the nobles. He was killed and put an end to his first Lusignan reign at Cilicia.

people.nombre: Juan de Lusignan, regent of Armenia
people.resumen: Son of Amalric and Isabella, he administered Armenia during the transition to Lusignan rule and supported the candidacy of his brother Guy. His son Leo would be the last king to exercise effective rule over the Cilician kingdom.

He was elected after the murder of Constantine II in a realm threatened by the Mameluces. His government sought to hold the remaining squares through military and diplomatic arrangements. It belonged to a hyetumide collateral branch.

He ruled during the final contraction of the kingdom and tried to find support against the Mamluk pressure. The internal divisions persisted and ended his murder. The crown later passed to Leon de Lusignan.

Last effective king of Cilician Armenia lost Sis to the Mamelucos in 1375 and spent years captive. He was released and went through European courts and sought support. His stay in Castile and his death in Paris connect the end of the kingdom with Western Europe.

eventos.titulo: L'Aquila: fall of Braccio da Montone

eventos.titulo: The Prince arrives at Lorenzo de’ Medici

eventos.titulo: Catherine of Medici directs the monarchy
eventos.descripcion: After the death of Francis II, Charles IX ascends the throne while being a minor. Catherine tries to uphold the royal authority between the Catholic party of the Guise and an increasingly organized Protestant nobility.
The massacre of Protestants in Wassy by the Duke of Guise's men accelerates the uprising led by Louis de Condé and opens the first of the French Wars of Religion.

A few days after the wedding of Margarita de Valois and Enrique de Navarra, the attempted murder of Coligny leads to the killing of Huguenot leaders in Paris and a new wave of violence for the kingdom.

The revolution in France upsets the European political balance and makes the fate of Marie Antoinette, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe

Philip Melanchthon presents Charles V with a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Escaleld League and captures its two great leaders, but military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.

Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche Condado, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Güeldres in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. Since 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

name: Penthièvre
summary: Penthièvre was a Breton county heritage whose line acquired decisive importance in the dispute over the duchy. Guy, son of Arthur II of Brittany, left a daughter, Joan, who married Charles de Blois. When John III died in 1341, Joan defended her position against John de Montfort. Her comital rights and ducal claim must be distinguished: the outcome of the succession war did not automatically disappear the heritage of Penthièvre. The connection with Châtillon came from the marriage of Joan and Charles, not from a male branch common to both houses.
